  60 | ## Small explanation of the mess below :)
  61 | #
  62 | # The previous version of the LaTeX formatter just assigned a command to
  63 | # each token type defined in the current style.  That obviously is
  64 | # problematic if the highlighted code is produced for a different style
  65 | # than the style commands themselves.
  66 | #
  67 | # This version works much like the HTML formatter which assigns multiple
  68 | # CSS classes to each <span> tag, from the most specific to the least
  69 | # specific token type, thus falling back to the parent token type if one
  70 | # is not defined.  Here, the classes are there too and use the same short
  71 | # forms given in token.STANDARD_TYPES.
  72 | #
  73 | # Highlighted code now only uses one custom command, which by default is
  74 | # \PY and selectable by the commandprefix option (and in addition the
  75 | # escapes \PYZat, \PYZlb and \PYZrb which haven't been renamed for
  76 | # backwards compatibility purposes).
  77 | #
  78 | # \PY has two arguments: the classes, separated by +, and the text to
  79 | # render in that style.  The classes are resolved into the respective
  80 | # style commands by magic, which serves to ignore unknown classes.
  81 | #
  82 | # The magic macros are:
  83 | # * \PY@it, \PY@bf, etc. are unconditionally wrapped around the text
  84 | #   to render in \PY@do.  Their definition determines the style.
  85 | # * \PY@reset resets \PY@it etc. to do nothing.
  86 | # * \PY@toks parses the list of classes, using magic inspired by the
  87 | #   keyval package (but modified to use plusses instead of commas
  88 | #   because fancyvrb redefines commas inside its environments).
  89 | # * \PY@tok processes one class, calling the \PY@tok@classname command
  90 | #   if it exists.
  91 | # * \PY@tok@classname sets the \PY@it etc. to reflect the chosen style
  92 | #   for its class.
  93 | # * \PY resets the style, parses the classnames and then calls \PY@do.
  94 | #
  95 | # Tip: to read this code, print it out in substituted form using e.g.
  96 | # >>> print STYLE_TEMPLATE % {'cp': 'PY'}

 157 |         \begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

 159 |             \PY{k}{pass}

 163 |

 165 |     are output by the `get_style_defs` method.

 464 | class LatexEmbeddedLexer(Lexer):
 465 |     """
 466 |     This lexer takes one lexer as argument, the lexer for the language
 467 |     being formatted, and the left and right delimiters for escaped text.
 468 | 
 469 |     First everything is scanned using the language lexer to obtain
 470 |     strings and comments. All other consecutive tokens are merged and
 471 |     the resulting text is scanned for escaped segments, which are given
 472 |     the Token.Escape type. Finally text that is not escaped is scanned
 473 |     again with the language lexer.
 474 |     """
 475 |     def __init__(self, left, right, lang, **options):
 476 |         self.left = left
 477 |         self.right = right
 478 |         self.lang = lang
 479 |         Lexer.__init__(self, **options)
 480 | 
 481 |     def get_tokens_unprocessed(self, text):
 482 |         # find and remove all the escape tokens (replace with an empty string)
 483 |         # this is very similar to DelegatingLexer.get_tokens_unprocessed.
 484 |         buffered = ''
 485 |         insertions = []
 486 |         insertion_buf = []
 487 |         for i, t, v in self._find_safe_escape_tokens(text):
 488 |             if t is None:
 489 |                 if insertion_buf:
 490 |                     insertions.append((len(buffered), insertion_buf))
 491 |                     insertion_buf = []
 492 |                 buffered += v
 493 |             else:
 494 |                 insertion_buf.append((i, t, v))
 495 |         if insertion_buf:
 496 |             insertions.append((len(buffered), insertion_buf))
 497 |         return do_insertions(insertions,
 498 |                              self.lang.get_tokens_unprocessed(buffered))
 499 | 
 500 |     def _find_safe_escape_tokens(self, text):
 501 |         """ find escape tokens that are not in strings or comments """
 502 |         for i, t, v in self._filter_to(
 503 |             self.lang.get_tokens_unprocessed(text),
 504 |             lambda t: t in Token.Comment or t in Token.String
 505 |         ):
 506 |             if t is None:
 507 |                 for i2, t2, v2 in self._find_escape_tokens(v):
 508 |                     yield i + i2, t2, v2
 509 |             else:
 510 |                 yield i, None, v
 511 | 
 512 |     def _filter_to(self, it, pred):
 513 |         """ Keep only the tokens that match `pred`, merge the others together """
 514 |         buf = ''
 515 |         idx = 0
 516 |         for i, t, v in it:
 517 |             if pred(t):
 518 |                 if buf:
 519 |                     yield idx, None, buf
 520 |                     buf = ''
 521 |                 yield i, t, v
 522 |             else:
 523 |                 if not buf:
 524 |                     idx = i
 525 |                 buf += v
 526 |         if buf:
 527 |             yield idx, None, buf
 528 | 
 529 |     def _find_escape_tokens(self, text):
 530 |         """ Find escape tokens within text, give token=None otherwise """
 531 |         index = 0
 532 |         while text:
 533 |             a, sep1, text = text.partition(self.left)
 534 |             if a:
 535 |                 yield index, None, a
 536 |                 index += len(a)
 537 |             if sep1:
 538 |                 b, sep2, text = text.partition(self.right)
 539 |                 if sep2:
 540 |                     yield index + len(sep1), Token.Escape, b
 541 |                     index += len(sep1) + len(b) + len(sep2)
 542 |                 else:
 543 |                     yield index, Token.Error, sep1
 544 |                     index += len(sep1)
 545 |                     text = b
